request: add the latest DSA and system design questions from open-source repos as lessons
title: Design a chat app like WhatsApp

problem.statement: Design a chat service like WhatsApp: people send text messages one-to-one and in small groups, and see whether their messages were delivered and read.
example: 1:1 chats and groups of up to 256 people
Messages reach people who were offline once they return
constraints: 500 million daily users, ~40 messages each a day
Under 200 ms between two online phones
No message is ever lost or shown out of order
problem.followUp: How does a message reach someone whose phone is switched off?

steps.caption: What the interviewer is really asking.

plain.asking: Get a message from one phone to another *instantly if both are online, later if not*, without ever losing it or mixing up the order.
points: *Must work:* send; delivered and read ticks; groups; offline delivery.
*Must be fast:* under 200 ms between two online phones.

steps.caption: Simplest idea: Bob’s phone asks the server *“anything new?”* every few seconds. Nearly every answer is “no”, and 100 million phones asking burns servers for nothing.
Better: every phone keeps one connection *open*, a WebSocket. Nobody asks; the server pushes a message down it the instant one arrives.
Alice sends “hi”. It goes up her open connection, and the server pushes it straight down Bob’s. Well under 200 ms.
100 million phones are online at once, each holding a connection open. One server can hold about 200,000. It falls over.
So run *hundreds of chat servers*. Alice is connected to A, Bob to C. But server A has Alice’s message and *no idea which server holds Bob*.

items.note: Holds Alice’s open connection, and ~200,000 others.

items.label: SERVER C
items.note: Holds Bob’s open connection.

check.question: Bob’s phone is off when Alice writes. Where does her message wait?
options: In Bob’s inbox in the message store
check.explain: The server keeps it until Bob’s phone *confirms* it, and the push notification tells his phone to reconnect and fetch it.
